questions.question: 'Dhangari Gaja' is a dance form mainly associated with _______.
questions.questionHtml: 'Dhangari Gaja' is a dance form mainly associated with _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

Key Points

  • Dhangari Gaja is one of Maharashtra's most colourful traditional folk dances.
  • The shepherds, cowherds, buffalo keepers, and blanket weavers of Maharashtra's Sholapur district perform this wonderful kind of dance.
  • Shepherds and men who work in the fields are known as Dhangars in the local dialect. This is a popular art form among the Sholapur district's shepherds.

Additional Information

  • Maharashtra has a diverse range of dance styles.
  • Povada is a Maratha dance form that celebrates Shivaji Maharaj's lifetime accomplishments.
  • Tamasha is a popular folk dance that is performed throughout the state.

questions.question: The legendary Kuchipudi dancer Dr. Raja Reddy referred to one of the following as a 'Kaliyuga Satyabhama'?

questions.question: Which among the following is a dance performed by the devotees during the ceremonial worship of Murugan the Hindu God of war?

questions.solution: The dance performed by the devotees during the ceremonial worship of Murugan is called Kavadi attam. It is a form of Tamil folk dance and is popular in South India, especially Tamil Nadu. questions.question: Which of the following classical dances is referred to as the dance of the storytellers?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following classical dances is referred to as the dance of the storytellers?
questions.solution: Kathak is referred to as the dance of storytellers as it originated as a temple or village performance where dancers narrated stories from ancient scriptures. It is a solo performance where the dancer recites verses and executes them through movement.

questions.solution:
• Popir is one of the famous dance form performed in the state of Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.question: ‘Kunbi Dance’ is a popular dance associated with which Indian state?
questions.questionHtml: ‘Kunbi Dance’ is a popular dance associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution: The Kunbi dance is a tribal folk dance of the Kunbi community in Goa, depicting social themes. It is characterized by its simplicity and is performed during various social occasions. The Kunbi (or Kanbi) term refers to traditionally non-elite farmers in Western India. Additionally, the Cheraw or bamboo dance is a significant dance form in Mizoram, Lepcha is a renowned folk dance in Sikkim, and the Rouf dance is predominantly performed by women in the Kashmir valley. These dances highlight the cultural diversity and traditional practices of different Indian states.

questions.question: ‘Dekhni’ is a traditional dance form of:
questions.questionHtml: ‘Dekhni’ is a traditional dance form of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Goa.

  • Dekhni dance represents an attractive mixture of folk culture and Western music, danced mostly by Christian girls in fully Indian dress.
  • The gestures in the dance appear to have been borrowed from the Kathak and Bharata Natyam.
  • Dekhni in Konkani language means bewitching beauty.
  • Dekhni dance is one of the oldest dance forms of Goa.
  • Dekhni dance can be associated with those people who converted into Christianity from Hinduism during Portuguese rule.
  • Dekhni Dance is performed by a group of girls caring earthen oil lamps in their hands.
  • These girls are represented as the servants of God in this dance form. It represents the life of a devadasi.
  • Ghumat Drum is the main instrument used in this dance.

Additional Information

  • Hanv Saiba Poltodi Vetam is one of the most famous songs of Dekni dance.
  • It was written by Carlos Eugenio Ferreira.
  • This song was first published in 1895 in Paris and then in Goa in 1926.
  • This song talks about a dancer who wanted to cross the river but the boatman refused to take her because the river was very rough that day.

questions.question: Which of the following is a traditional masked dance of West Bengal?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a traditional masked dance of West Bengal?
questions.solution: The traditional masked dance of West Bengal is Gambhira, performed during the festival of Chaitra Sankranti by worshippers of Shakti. This dance is performed all over the Malda district of North Bengal. The dance is named so because it is performed in the dance hall of the Chandi Mandir - Gambhira, which has a specially constructed pavilion in front of the shrine, for the dance.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the ‘Jhora’ dance performed as a springtime celebration?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following states is the ‘Jhora’ dance performed as a springtime celebration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is UttarakhandKey Points

  • The Jhora dance is performed in the state of Uttarakhand as a springtime celebration
  • The Jhora dance originated in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand. 
  • The Jhora dance is typically performed in the spring season. 
  • The Jhora dance is also performed at weddings, festivals, and fairs. 

Additional Information

  • Community dance: The Jhora dance is a community dance that brings together people of all castes. 
  • Dance moves: The Jhora dance involves men and women moving in a circle, holding hands, and slightly bending forward.
    • Each step is taken with a slight jump and accompanied by neck and shoulder movements. 
  • Traditional drum: The Jhora dance is performed to the accompaniment of the traditional drum, known as the "Hurka".

questions.question: With which of the following states is the theatre form 'Maach' traditionally associated?
questions.questionHtml: With which of the following states is the theatre form 'Maach' traditionally associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

  • Maach is a well-known folk theatre form of Madhya Pradesh and history tells us that it has been an intrinsic part of the local culture of the Malwa region.

Key Points

  • its existence can be dated back to the early 18th century thus making it a 200–250-year-old art form.
  • Gopalji Guru of Bhagsipura, Ujjain, is proclaimed to be the person who introduced maach in Madhya Pradesh;
  • He eventually directed many maach plays himself.
  • Traditionally, it is performed around the Indian festival of Holi.
  • It is also believed that maach originated to entertain the local communities as there was no other mode of entertainment available at those times.

questions.question: Dhangari Gaja is a folk dance of ________.

questions.solution: Dhangari Gaja is a popular folk dance form of Maharashtra, which is performed during various festive occasions. The dance is performed by a group of male dancers who wear colorful traditional attire and play musical instruments like dhol, tasha, and cymbals.

questions.question: Due to the service done by the poet ___________, the Kathakali dance form received a new impetus and today, many innovations are also being made to suit the needs of a changing society.
questions.questionHtml: Due to the service done by the poet ___________, the Kathakali dance form received a new impetus and today, many innovations are also being made to suit the needs of a changing society.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vallathol Narayan Menon.

Key Points

  • Vallathol Narayana Menon was a poet in the Malayalam language.
  • He was one of the triumvirate poets of modern Malayalam, along with Kumaran Asan and Ulloor S. Parameswara Iyer.
  • He was a nationalist poet and wrote a series of poems on various aspects of the Indian freedom movement.
  • He also wrote against caste restriction, tyrannies and orthodoxies.
  • He founded the Kerala Kalamandalam.
  • He is credited with revitalizing the traditional Keralite dance form known as Kathakali.

Additional Information

  • Kathakali is a major form of classical Indian dance.
  • It is a "story play" genre of art.
  • It is native to the Malayalam-speaking southwestern region of Kerala.
  • It is entirely practiced and appreciated by Malayali people.
  • The famous dancers of Kathakali include Kalamandalam Gopi, Kalamandalam Krishna Prasad, Kottakal Sivaraman, Kalamandalam Ramankutty Nair, Kalamandalam Vasu Pisharody, Kavungal Chathunni Panicker.

questions.question: Which form of dance involves balancing pots on the head of the dancer?
questions.questionHtml: Which form of dance involves balancing pots on the head of the dancer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhavai.

Key Points

  • Bhavai form of dance involves balancing pots on the head of the dancer.
  • Bhavai Dance is a very difficult form of dance performed by skilled experts.
  • In this dance, women dancers balance 8 to 9 pitchers on their heads and dance simultaneously.
  • And sway with the soles of their feet perched on the top of a glass and also sometimes on the edge of a naked sword.
  • This dance is believed to be originated in Gujarat.
  • And was soon picked up and adopted by the local tribal men and women of Rajasthan.
  • This is basically performed by the women of the Jat, Bhil, Raigar, Meena, Kumhar, and Kalbelia communities of Rajasthan.
  • Main instruments:
    • Dholak, Jhanjhar, Pakhwaja, Sarangi, and Harmonium (played in background music).
    • The government is taking all necessary measures to revive this fast-dying tradition of folk dance.

Additional Information

  • Cheraw:
    • It is one of the traditional and oldest dances of Mizoram.
    • It is also recognized as the oldest dance form of Mizoram.
    • It is also known as the Bamboo dance.
    • It is one of the most famous dances in Mizoram, and a centre of attraction during festive occasions.
    • Chewar is performed by six to eight people holding a pair of bamboo staves on another horizontally placed bamboo on the ground on special occasions such as when there is a bumper harvest of a crop. Gongs and drums are used as a musical instruments in Cheraw dance.
  • Deodhani:
    • It is a dance form of Assam.

questions.question: The 'Loor dance' is a traditional folk dance, performed only by women, in the state of:

questions.solution: The 'Loor dance' is a traditional folk dance, performed only by women, in the state of Haryana. It is specially performed during the Holi festival. This dance marks the arrival of the pleasant spring season and with it the harvesting of the Rabi crops in the farms. Girls usually participate in this dance wearing their traditional dress of Ghagra, Kurti, Chundri, and Chunda.

  • The Koya people are said to have migrated to central India from their original home in Bastar, Northern India.
  • They believe that their main deity still resides in a cave in the Bastar region. 
  • The Koya language, also called Koyi and is closely related to Gondi and has been strongly influenced by Telugu.
  • Most Koya speaks either Gondi or Telugu, in addition to Koyi.
  • The Koya people are primarily farmers.

Additional Information

questions.question: With which of the following states is the dance form 'Povadas associated'?
questions.questionHtml: With which of the following states is the dance form 'Povadas associated'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

Key Points

  • Povadas dance form is associated with Maharashtra state.
  • Povadas are presented in the Marathi ballad form.
  • This dance form describes the events in the life of the great Maratha ruler, Shri Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
  • The word Povada itself means "the narration of a story in glorious terms".
  • The narratives are always odes in praise of an individual hero or an incident or place.
  • The chief narrator is known as the Shahir who plays the duff to keep the rhythm.
  • The tempo is fast and controlled by the main singer who is supported by others in the chorus.
  • The earliest notable Powada was the Afzal Khanacha Vadh (The Killing of Afzal Khan) (1659) by Agnidas which recorded Shivaji's encounter with Afzal Khan.
  • Dhangari Gaja, Koli Dance, Lavani Dance, Povadas Dance, and Tamasha are other dance forms of Maharashtra state. 

Additional Information

  • Dance forms of Karnataka:
    • Kunitha, Yakshagana, Sannatas, Parijata, Doddatas, etc.
  • Dance forms of Kerala:
    • Theyyam, Thiruvathirakali, Chakyar Koothu Koodiyattam, Ottamthullal, Mohiniyattam, Kathakali, Padayani, etc.
  • Dance forms of Tamilnadu:
    • Kumi, Kollatam, Mayil attam, Pulliyattam, Bharathnatyam etc.

questions.question: The 'Dhangari Gaja' traditional folk dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.questionHtml: The 'Dhangari Gaja' traditional folk dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

Key Points

  • Dhangari Gaja
    • It is reckoned among the vibrant traditional folk dances of Maharashtra. Hence, Option 2 is correct.
    • This exquisite form of dance belongs to the shepherds, cowherds, buffalo keepers, and blanket weavers of Sholapur district, Maharashtra.
    • Shepherds and men who undertake husbandry are referred to as Dhangars in the local dialect.
    • This art form is common among the shepherd community of Sholapur district.
    • The cowherds, buffalo keepers, weavers, and sheep and goat keepers have to stay away from their families for a long time because of the nature of their occupation.
    • During work, they spend most of their time close to nature.
    • Being in the beautiful surroundings of nature and drawing inspiration from its grandeur, they write poems in the form of couplets.
    • Their poetry is called ovi which along with representing their love for nature also unfolds their dedication towards God Biruba.
    • When these shepherds return home, they celebrate their time with family and loved ones performing Dhangari Gaja dance on the beats of drums accompanied with the recitation of their poems.
    • Through this dance, they also ask for blessings from their God.

Additional Information

questions.question: Janaki Prasad is associated with which Gharana of Kathak?
questions.questionHtml: Janaki Prasad is associated with which Gharana of Kathak?
questions.solution: Janaki Prasad is associated with the Banaras Gharana of Kathak, which is known for its intricate footwork and graceful movements. This gharana originated in the city of Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh and is characterized by its emphasis on layakari (rhythmic play) tandava (masculine) and lasya (feminine) elements.The Banaras Gharana is known for its intricate footwork and graceful movements.

questions.question: _________ is a mask dance popular in South Malabar.
questions.questionHtml: _________ is a mask dance popular in South Malabar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kummattikali.

Key Points

  • Kummattikali also known as Kummatti is a colourful mask dance of Kerala prevalent in Thrissur District, Palakkad District, and parts of South Malabar.
  • It is mainly performed on the occasion of the Onam festival(the New year of the Malayalam calendar).
  • During the Onam festival, people perform this dance while visiting the houses of various people across the town and the cities to collect small gifts and entertain people while walking across the streets.
  • The dancers wear heavily painted colourful wooden masks depicting the faces of Krishna, Narada, Kiratha, and Darika.
  • These masks are usually made out of saprophyte, jack fruit tree.

Additional Information

  • The themes of Kummattikali are mostly taken from the stories of Ramayana, Darika Vadham, the story of Shiva, and folk tales like Manjan Nayare Pattu.

questions.question: Minati Mishra was conferred the Padma Shree for her contribution to which form of dance?
questions.questionHtml: Minati Mishra was conferred the Padma Shree for her contribution to which form of dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Odissi.

Key Points

  • Minati Mishra was a renowned Indian classical dancer known for her contributions to the Odissi dance form.
  • She was conferred the Padma Shree, one of India's highest civilian awards, in 2012 for her significant contributions to Odissi.
  • Odissi is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, originating from the state of Odisha.
  • Minati Mishra was not only a performer but also a teacher and choreographer, contributing immensely to the promotion and preservation of Odissi.

Additional Information

  • Odissi Dance:
    • Odissi is characterized by its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculpturesque poses.
    • It is traditionally performed by women, and its themes are usually religious, often inspired by the Vaishnavism sect.
    • Odissi is known for its Tribhangi posture, which divides the body into three parts: head, bust, and torso.
    • The dance form includes both pure dance (Nritta) and expressive dance (Abhinaya).
  • Padma Shree Award:
    • The Padma Shree is the fourth highest civilian award in India.
    • It is awarded to citizens of India in recognition of their distinguished contribution in various spheres of activity, including the arts.
    • The award is announced on Republic Day (26th January) each year.
  • Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra:
    • He is considered one of the foremost exponents of Odissi dance.
    • His contributions have been instrumental in reviving and popularizing the dance form in modern times.
  • Classical Dance Forms of India:
    • India is home to several classical dance forms, each with its unique style and cultural significance.
    • Other major classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.

questions.question: The cultural heritage of Siddhis from _________ dates back to almost 300 years and their Siddhi Dhamal dance is an exquisite art form.
questions.questionHtml: The cultural heritage of Siddhis from _________ dates back to almost 300 years and their Siddhi Dhamal dance is an exquisite art form.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

Key Points

- The **Siddhis** are an ethnic group in India, primarily found in the state of **Gujarat**. - Their cultural heritage dates back to almost **300 years**. - The **Siddhi Dhamal dance** is a notable art form that is unique to this community. - The Siddhis are believed to have **African** origins and have preserved many elements of their ancestral culture.

Additional Information

- **Siddhis** are descendants of African slaves, sailors, and traders who settled in India. - They are known for their **distinctive music and dance forms**, which blend African and Indian elements. - The **Siddhi Dhamal dance** is performed during religious ceremonies and festivals. - The Siddhis have made significant contributions to the **cultural diversity** of Gujarat. - The community is also found in **Karnataka** and **Maharashtra**, but Gujarat has the largest population.

questions.question: Which one of the following dances are associated with the Vaishnavism of the Meitai people?
questions.questionHtml: Which one of the following dances are associated with the Vaishnavism of the Meitai people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

Key Points

  • Manipuri
    • Manipuri dance is the main classical dance form of India.
    • The Manipuri language is named after its native place Manipur.
    • The dance is based on Hindu Vaishnava themes and culminates with the love story of Radha and Krishna.
    • The dance form is slow-moving and graceful, with the arms flowing to the fingers in a symbolic splendor.
    • This dance form is based on its early customs and magical dance forms.
    • Themes from the works of Vishnu Purana, Bhagavata Purana, and Gita Govinda are mainly used in this.

Additional Information

  • Chhau
    • Chhau is a folk dance practiced in the states of West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand.
    • There are three types – Seraikela Chhau, Mayurbhanj Chhau and Purulia Chhau.
    • This dance is a mixture of Samprik custom and dance and it depicts fighting techniques and animal movements and movements.
    • This dance is performed by male dancers who are traditional artists or people of the local community.
  • Sattriya
    • Sattriya dance is a classical dance form of Assam.
    • The founder of this dance is the great saint Srimanta Sankardev.
    • This dance form is a tradition going on for more than 500 years.
    • This dance is a tradition of the Vaishnava monasteries of Assam, known as Satra.
  • Kuchipudi
    • Kuchipudi is a famous dance form in Andhra Pradesh, India.
    • It is famous all over South India.
    • The dance derives its name from the village Kuchipudi in Divi taluk of Krishna district, where Brahmins reside in this traditional dance practice.
    • According to tradition, the Kuchipudi dance was originally performed only by men and that too only by men from the Brahmin community.

    • This community is an indigenous people of the Himalayan region, with a population of around 11,000.

questions.question: The “Nalacharitam” play is associated with which Indian dance form?
questions.questionHtml: The “Nalacharitam” play is associated with which Indian dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

Key Points

  • Nalacharitam is a play that originated in the state of Kerala, which is known for its rich cultural heritage and traditional dance forms.
  • Nalacharitham was written by Unnayi Warrier in the 18th century. 
  • The play Nalacharitam is a popular performance in Kathakali, which tells the story of King Nala and his struggles.​

Important Points

  • Kathakali is a classical Indian dance form which is a story play genre of art is the folk dance form of Kerala.
  • It is a combination of 5 forms of fine art which are –
    • Natyam (expressions)
    • Nritham (dance)
    • Nrithyam (enactment) 
    • Sangeetam (music)
    • Vadya (instruments)
  • Various costumes of characters of Kathakali –
    • Sathwika (Hero)
    • Katti (Villain)
    • Minukku (females)
    • Thathi (other characters)
  • Types of Drums used in Kathakali – Maddalam, Chenda, and Idakka
  • Kathakali is the most difficult style of the traditional dance form in which actors speak ‘sign language’ where hand gestures are used to dictate word part of the character and facial and eye movements express emotions and mood.
  • Kathakali is based on the epics of Ramayana and Mahabharata. 

Additional Information

  • Kathak, on the other hand, is a classical dance form that originated in North India and is known for its intricate footwork and graceful movements.
  • Sattriya is a classical dance form from the state of Assam.
  • Odissi is a classical dance form from the state of Odisha.
